topic_summary: Analysis of the euthanasia debate as a contested kernel where the end-of-life decision framework is read through either autonomy-primary or sanctity-of-life-primary lenses. Each reading produces structurally different constraints with distinct victim sets: the suffering-prolonged (denied relief) versus the pressured-vulnerable (coerced into death). The kernel contest centers on whether individual self-determination or life preservation takes interpretive priority in medical ethics.

key_entities: Terminally ill patients requesting euthanasia (primary rights-claimants in autonomy reading)
Vulnerable populations (elderly, disabled, mentally ill) (primary victims in sanctity reading)
Legal jurisdictions (Belgium, Netherlands, Canada, 14 US states) (authority structures)
key_tensions: Individual autonomy vs collective protection (autonomy reading vs sanctity reading)
Physician as healer vs physician as death-facilitator (professional identity)
Compassionate relief vs slippery slope risk (beneficence vs non-maleficence)
key_mechanisms: Legal eligibility criteria (gatekeeping mechanism in autonomy-permitting jurisdictions)
Coercion pressure (systemic vulnerability mechanism in sanctity reading)
Psychiatric disability expansion (scope creep mechanism in Belgium/Netherlands)
key_absences: Palliative care infrastructure quality (alternative to euthanasia not examined in source)
Economic incentives in healthcare systems (cost-saving pressure on vulnerable populations)

axes.structural_delta: Individual right to choose death with dignity takes interpretive priority; suffering-prolonged are victims of denial
axes.primary_observable: Legal eligibility criteria emphasizing competent consent; patient autonomy as first-order principle in medical ethics codes
axes.selection_reason: Core reading of contested kernel; distinct victim set and constraint structure
axes.interpretive_commitment: Competent individuals possess sovereign authority over their own death; state/medical authority exists to facilitate, not override, this choice
axes.authority_grounding: Liberal individualism; Enlightenment autonomy tradition (Hume, Kant); patient rights movement
axes.expected_structural_delta: Suffering-prolonged enter victim set when denied access; healthcare professionals become facilitators rather than gatekeepers; slippery slope risk externalized as acceptable cost

axes.structural_delta: Intrinsic value of human life takes interpretive priority; pressured-vulnerable are victims of coercion
axes.primary_observable: Legal prohibition regimes; physician role definitions emphasizing life preservation; religious doctrine on life sanctity
axes.selection_reason: Core reading of contested kernel; distinct victim set and constraint structure; axiomatically contradictory to autonomy reading
axes.interpretive_commitment: Human life possesses intrinsic value independent of individual will; intentional life-ending violates this value regardless of consent
axes.authority_grounding: Religious tradition (Christian sanctity doctrine); Hippocratic oath; deontological ethics
axes.expected_structural_delta: Pressured-vulnerable enter victim set when euthanasia is available; physician role becomes healer-only; individual suffering externalized as necessary cost of life protection

axes.structural_delta: Protection of vulnerable populations from systemic coercion takes interpretive priority; both suffering-prolonged and pressured-vulnerable are victims of inadequate safeguards
axes.primary_observable: Eligibility criteria complexity; psychiatric disability expansion rates (Belgium/Netherlands); palliative care infrastructure investment
axes.selection_reason: Hybrid reading attempting to reconcile kernel contest; distinct structural delta focusing on institutional design rather than foundational axioms
axes.interpretive_commitment: End-of-life authority must be distributed across multiple institutional checkpoints to prevent both denial of relief and coercive pressure
axes.authority_grounding: Institutional design theory; harm reduction frameworks; disability rights advocacy
axes.expected_structural_delta: Dual victim set acknowledged; constraint focuses on procedural safeguards rather than categorical permission/prohibition; slippery slope becomes empirical question rather than axiom

omegas.description: Is the autonomy vs sanctity contest a false binary masking inadequate palliative care investment? If high-quality pain management were universally available, would the suffering-prolonged victim set shrink to near-zero, collapsing the autonomy reading's empirical foundation?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — palliative care quality not examined in source material

omegas.description: Do healthcare cost pressures create systemic coercion independent of individual choice architecture? If vulnerable populations face implicit pressure to choose death due to care costs, the vulnerability-protection reading may underestimate extractiveness.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — economic incentives absent from source material

omegas.description: Does the Nazi euthanasia program's historical shadow function as a piton (atrophied discourse) preventing legitimate autonomy claims, or as a mountain (genuine risk signal) validating sanctity concerns? The kernel contest may be distorted by this unresolved historical trauma.
omegas.source: Extraction anchor (Nazi program) + F03 concern about mountain classification

omegas.description: Is psychiatric disability euthanasia (Belgium/Netherlands) a slippery slope confirmation or a legitimate autonomy extension? commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The end-of-life decision authority kernel: who holds legitimate authority to determine when and how a human life may intentionally end
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between individual (autonomy reading), divine/natural law (sanctity reading), and institutional safeguard designers (vulnerability-protection reading). No single interpretive authority; jurisdictional fragmentation.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Autonomy reading holds individual will as sovereign over life/death decisions; sanctity reading holds life value as independent of and superior to individual will. No coherent framework can simultaneously hold both that individual consent makes intentional killing permissible AND that life's intrinsic value makes intentional killing impermissible regardless of consent.
